A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAVE, retaining identifiable concept-extraction, neural-volume classification and attribution foundations despite the changed title and substantial revision. The main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and interpretability results in Tables 2–3, alongside concept-extraction ablations and qualitative evaluations in its supplement.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and interpretability results, plus pose-estimation, volume-shape and attribution experiments in Tables C1–C2, F1–F3 and G1.

M1.justification: v1 uses cuboid volumes trained with annotated poses. v2 Section 4.2 introduces training with Orient-Anything estimated poses and adopts ellipsoid volumes, also supporting more expressive CAD geometries. These materially change training inputs and object representations; the underlying K-Means concept extraction, concept matching and NOV-aware LRP remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on ImageNet3D, extending the original Pascal-based coverage to many additional object categories. It also evaluates orientation estimation and explicitly examines multi-object scenes in Appendices C and I. Pascal3D+, OccludedP3D+, OOD-CV and Pascal-Part remain represented.

E2.justification: v2 removes CRAFT, MCD, ICE and PCX from the classification-accuracy comparison, where they appeared in v1 Table 3, while retaining them for interpretability evaluation. Appendix G expands the original vanilla-LRP contrast with evaluated Guided Backpropagation, SmoothGrad, GradCAM and Integrated Gradients comparators.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets change from 100 to 200 epochs for ProtoPNet/TesNet and from 60 to 200 main-training epochs for PIP-Net; MCD's completeness threshold changes from 0.7 to 0.9. v2 drops the ConvNext PIP-Net configuration, introduces estimated-pose evaluation and revises 3D-C. Pureness is removed, while local coverage survives as spatial localisation. New pose-tolerance and controlled geometry experiments add further protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds estimated-versus-annotated pose comparisons, four-shape ablations, quantitative attribution comparisons and multi-object, symmetry and OOD failure analyses. Accuracy-versus-concept-count sweeps replace v1's reconstruction-quality-versus-count plot. The original concept-space separation and extraction-method analyses are retained in Appendix H, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 Figures J6–J9 newly specify seed 42 for randomly selecting concepts and example images; v1 gives no corresponding seed information. This is limited seed disclosure for qualitative sampling. Neither version reports repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial ImageNet3D, pose, geometry and attribution results. The reported OOD-CV ranking changes from LF-CBM 83.6% versus CAVE 81.4% in v1 Table 3 to CAVE 80.4% versus LF-CBM 73.5% in v2 Table 2. Method and training settings differ, so this is not a same-setting improvement. Pascal-Part accuracy and v1's complete class-wise 3D-C table are no longer reported.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5 revises the existing 3D-C definition by explicitly normalising concept attributions and using the number of images containing a concept in its denominator, alongside converting dissimilarity to similarity. The 50% frequency filter and core dictionary-learning/LRP mathematics already existed in v1. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 expands CAVE's central applicability claim to training without ground-truth pose annotations and redefines its proposed representation around ellipsoid volumes. In v1, annotated poses and cuboid approximation were explicit limitations, with pose estimation only suggested as a workaround. The joint robustness, interpretability and NOV-aware attribution claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops applicability boundaries and mechanisms: pose-estimator errors, geometry-versus-scalability tradeoffs, missed instances from object-centric training, and concept ambiguity under symmetry or deformation. Appendix B additionally explains how canonical meshes can smooth fine details and miss intra-class shape variation. These replace or extend v1's largely prospective pose and cuboid limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a CAVE code link, a detailed training-hyperparameter table, H100 training times, Gaussian-visibility filtering details and mesh projection/rendering instructions. These greatly expand v1's sparse CAVE implementation documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed step changed. Conversely, v1's exact filtered Pascal-Part sample-count table is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning around training without annotated poses and evaluating concepts without predefined part labels. New discussions cite Orient-Anything and concept-evaluation work by Huang, Behzadi-Khormouji and Oramas, and Zhu. This broadens the argument beyond v1's positioning around robust NOVUM classification and concept discovery, while retaining NOVUM as the foundation.

P1.justification: The Plato's cave framing is removed from the title and narrative, and substantial introductory and explanatory passages are rewritten. v2 separates NOVUM preliminaries, CAVE and 3D consistency into dedicated sections, moves detailed LRP material to Appendix A, combines discussion and conclusion, and reorganises the supplement into indexed Appendices A–K.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The opening illustration and method pipeline are redesigned, benchmark tables gain supervision and dataset groupings, and new geometry, pose, attribution and failure-case displays are added. Qualitative explanations receive extensive visual redesign; retained concept-space plots are relocated to Appendix H.

improvement.justification: v2 turns v1's suggested workaround for pose annotations into a tested method and substantially strengthens validation through ImageNet3D, controlled geometry experiments and quantitative attribution comparisons. Expanded implementation details and concrete failure analyses improve reproducibility and clarify applicability. Estimated poses incur accuracy losses, explicitly documented in Table C2, and some implementation descriptions remain inconsistent, including two versus three upsampling layers. Nevertheless, the demonstrated reduction in annotation dependence and stronger validation provide substantial overall gains.
